SC10-01.q: Which solution is used to identify starch?
SC10-01.expl: Iodine gives a blue–black colour with starch.

SC10-01.q: Which element is always present in proteins but absent in carbohydrates?
SC10-01.expl: Carbohydrates contain only C, H, O; proteins also contain N.

SC10-01.q: Which condition is essential to get a positive Benedict's test?
SC10-01.expl: The Benedict's test gives a brick-red precipitate only when heated in a water bath.

SC10-01.q: In which form are carbohydrates stored in animals?
SC10-01.expl: Stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles.

SC10-01.q: Why does an enzyme's activity drop after heating it to 80 °C?
SC10-01.expl: High temperature changes the protein structure (denaturation).

SC10-01.q: Which of the following is not a polymer?
SC10-01.expl: Glucose is a monosaccharide (a monomer).

SC10-01.q: A food sample gave purple with Biuret and brown with iodine. The sample contains?
SC10-01.expl: Purple → protein present; iodine did not change colour → no starch.

SC10-01.q: Biological importance of water being a good solvent?
opts: It helps transport substances and acts as a medium for reactions
SC10-01.expl: Substances are transported and react in dissolved form.

SC10-01.q: Since fats are insoluble in water, they are important as?
opts: A component of the cell membrane
SC10-01.expl: Lipids are a major component of membranes.

SC10-01.q: Salivary amylase in humans converts starch into?
SC10-01.expl: Amylase converts starch into maltose (a disaccharide).

SC10-01.q: C₆H₁₂O₆ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O — when this equation is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients, the coefficient of O₂?
SC10-01.expl: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O (atom count checked; File 7: EQ-042).

SC10-01.q: The compound present in the largest amount in the body?
SC10-01.expl: About 60–70% of body mass is water.

SC10-01.q: Structural unit of proteins?
SC10-01.expl: Amino acids are joined by peptide bonds.

SC10-01.q: What is obtained when lipids are hydrolysed?
SC10-01.expl: Lipase breaks down lipids.

SC10-01.q: DNA and RNA are which type of biological molecule?
SC10-01.expl: Polymers made of nucleotides.

SC10-01.q: The reagent that turns starch blue-black?
SC10-01.expl: Iodine — starch test.

SC10-01.q: Which does not give a positive Benedict's test?
SC10-01.expl: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.

SC10-01.q: Storage polysaccharide in animals?
SC10-01.expl: Glycogen in the liver and muscles.

SC10-01.q: Enzymes are which type of molecule?
SC10-01.expl: Biological catalysts — proteins.

SC10-01.q: What can calcium deficiency cause in children?
opts: Weak bones and teeth (linked to rickets)
SC10-01.expl: Ca and vitamin D for bone formation.

SC10-01.q: Disease caused by iodine deficiency?
SC10-01.expl: Iodine for thyroxine production.

SC10-01.q: A symptom of vitamin A deficiency?
SC10-01.expl: Vitamin A for the retinal pigment.

SC10-01.q: Food component that gives the most energy per unit mass?
SC10-01.expl: Lipids give about twice the energy.

SC10-01.q: Why does an enzyme stop working at high temperature?
SC10-01.expl: Its three-dimensional shape is destroyed.

SC10-01.q: Which is not a biological importance of water?
SC10-01.expl: Water does not provide energy.

SC10-01.q: A positive Biuret test shows?
SC10-01.expl: Purple colour — peptide bonds.

SC10-06.q: Two parts found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
SC10-06.expl: The cell wall and chloroplasts are distinctive to plant cells.

SC10-06.q: Main site of ATP production?
SC10-06.expl: Aerobic respiration takes place in the mitochondria, producing ATP.

SC10-06.q: What controls the substances entering the cell?
SC10-06.expl: The cell membrane is selectively permeable.

SC10-06.q: Function of ribosomes?
SC10-06.expl: Ribosomes join amino acids to synthesise proteins.

SC10-06.q: Why do muscle cells have many mitochondria?
opts: They need a lot of energy
SC10-06.expl: Muscle contraction needs a lot of ATP.

SC10-06.q: Why do root cells lack chloroplasts?
opts: No light reaches them, so photosynthesis is not needed
Because there is no cell wall
SC10-06.expl: There is no light under the soil; chloroplasts are not needed.

SC10-06.q: Cell wall and cell membrane — the correct statement?
opts: The cell wall is fully permeable; the cell membrane is selectively permeable
The cell wall is selectively permeable
SC10-06.expl: The cell wall is a mesh of cellulose — fully permeable.

SC10-06.q: Which of the following belongs only to animal cells?
SC10-06.expl: Centrioles help in cell division; usually absent in higher plants.

SC10-06.q: Well developed in secretory cells (e.g. enzyme-secreting cells)?
SC10-06.expl: The Golgi apparatus packages and secretes.

SC10-06.q: Which is not clearly visible when onion epidermal cells are viewed under a light microscope?

SC10-06.q: In the Plant cell diagram, what is the function of the 'Cell membrane'?
opts: Controls the entry and exit of substances
SC10-06.expl: Cell membrane: Controls the entry and exit of substances (File 6: BIO-D01).

SC10-06.q: In the Plant cell diagram, what is the function of the 'Nucleus'?

SC10-06.expl: Nucleus: Controls cell activities; DNA (File 6: BIO-D01).

SC10-06.q: In the Animal cell diagram, what is the function of the 'Cell membrane'?
SC10-06.expl: Cell membrane: Controls entry and exit (File 6: BIO-D02).

SC10-06.q: In the Animal cell diagram, what is the function of the 'Nucleus'?
SC10-06.expl: Nucleus: Control centre (File 6: BIO-D02).

SC10-06.q: In the Animal cell diagram, what is the function of the 'Nucleolus'?
SC10-06.expl: Nucleolus: Makes ribosomes (File 6: BIO-D02).

SC10-06.q: Function of the ribosome?
SC10-06.expl: Ribosomes make proteins.

SC10-06.q: Movement of water through the cell membrane?
SC10-06.expl: Movement of water through a partially permeable membrane.

SC10-06.q: Movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration?
SC10-06.expl: Diffusion needs no energy.

SC10-06.q: A process that needs ATP to move substances against a concentration gradient?
SC10-06.expl: Transport that uses energy.

SC10-06.q: If a red blood cell is placed in water?
SC10-06.expl: No cell wall — it swells and bursts by osmosis.

SC10-06.q: Function of the Golgi body?
SC10-06.expl: Processing secretions.
